text: Exam notes on the Marathas, in the usual five parts: key facts, the explanation, a timeline, terms, and practice questions.

block.title: The Marathas, 1674 to 1818
block.because: The facts Prelims asks and the explanation Mains wants

sections.md:
- [[Shivaji|person]] was crowned Chhatrapati at [[Raigad|place]] in 1674 [E][S1].
- The [[Treaty of Purandar|event]] (1665) made Shivaji give 23 forts to the Mughals [E][S2].
- The [[Ashtapradhan|term]] was Shivaji's council of eight ministers, headed by the Peshwa [E][S1].
- [[Chauth|term]] was a levy of a quarter of a region's revenue; [[sardeshmukhi|term]] an extra tenth [E][S3].
- [[Baji Rao I|person]], Peshwa from 1720 to 1740, carried Maratha power into north India [E].
- The Marathas lost the [[Third Battle of Panipat|event]] to Ahmad Shah Abdali in 1761 [E][S4].
- The [[Treaty of Salbai|event]] (1782) ended the First Anglo-Maratha War [E].
- The Third Anglo-Maratha War ended the Peshwa's rule in 1818 [E][S5].

block.title: The Marathas: the dates to know
Terms
block.because: The words an exam asks you to explain
block.md:
- **Chhatrapati**: the title Shivaji took at his coronation, "lord of the umbrella" [E].
- **Ashtapradhan**: the council of eight ministers [E][S1].
- **Peshwa**: the chief minister, who became the real ruler after 1713 [E].
- **Chauth**: a quarter of the revenue, paid to escape Maratha raids [E][S3].
- **Sardeshmukhi**: a further tenth, claimed as hereditary right [E][S3].

items.stem: Consider the following statements about the Marathas: 1. Chauth was a levy of one-fourth of the revenue. 2. The Third Battle of Panipat was fought in 1761. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.why: Chauth was a quarter of the revenue, and Panipat was fought in January 1761.

items.stem: Match the treaty with its year
items.explain: Purandar with the Mughals (1665); Salbai ended the first war with the British (1782); Bassein brought the subsidiary alliance (1802).

sections.md: Shivaji built a state in the hills of the western Deccan, where forts and light cavalry beat larger armies [E][S1]. He paid his soldiers in cash rather than with land grants, which kept them loyal to the state [L]. After Aurangzeb's death in 1707 the Mughal grip loosened, and the Peshwas turned chauth and sardeshmukhi into a claim on half of India's revenue [E][S3].

sections.h: Why they lost at Panipat, and then to the British
sections.md: At Panipat in 1761 the Maratha army was far from its supply lines and had few allies in the north [E][S4]. The defeat weakened the Peshwa's hold over the great Maratha chiefs, the Sindhias, Holkars, Gaekwads and Bhonsles [L]. Divided, they were defeated one by one: the Treaty of Bassein (1802) made the Peshwa accept a subsidiary alliance, and 1818 ended his rule [E][S5].

**Mains:** "Assess the role of the Peshwas in the expansion of Maratha power in the eighteenth century. (150 words)"

A good answer names Baji Rao I's campaigns in the north, the chauth and sardeshmukhi claims, the weakness Panipat exposed, and ends with why the confederacy split.

card.front: When was Shivaji crowned, and where?

card.back: A levy of a quarter of a region's revenue, paid to escape Maratha raids.
A further tenth of the revenue, claimed as a hereditary right.

card.front: Which treaty ended the First Anglo-Maratha War?
Why did the Maratha chiefs fall to the British one by one after Panipat?
card.back: Panipat weakened the Peshwa's hold, so the great chiefs acted alone and could be defeated separately.
